page.layout: One page of text, no margins. Top: a woodcut ornament strip (not text), then a centred dedication heading in capitals and small capitals. Below: a poem of verse lines, begun by a large woodcut initial O. At the foot: a signature mark "*2" at the right of the text block.

main_text.head: AD ILLVSTRISSIMVM, ET POTENTISSIMVM PRINCIPEM, ac Dominum D. Ioannem Casimirū, Comitem Palatinum ad Rhenum, Electoralis Palatinatus Tutorem & administratorem, Ducem Bauariae, &c. Dominum clementissimum.
main_text.p: OVÆ cura Vatū, quæ lyra te placens Reddat venusto carmine lucidum: Tuasque virtutes in ævum Per memores CASIMIRE fastos Æternet? O, quæ CALLIOPE mori Dignos peremni laude vetas viros Descende PARNASSO virenti, Perpetuumque melos recense: Quod clara tanti nomina PRINCIPIS Monstret per orbem: quâ nitet aureus Ardente sol curru, suosque Candidior iaculatur ignes Terras amoeno lumine recreans. Hic ille doctas PEGASIDUM videt Lætus choreas, atque dulces

page.notes: The woodcut initial is an O, read as the first letter of the poem; the first word is printed as "V Æ" and is given as VÆ with [?] advised, since the printed line may read differently. Italic lines are the poem; the capitalised words CASIMIRE, CALLIOPE, PARNASSO, PRINCIPIS, PEGASIDUM are set in roman small capitals. The poem continues on the following page. The woodcut strip at the top is decoration and is not transcribed.
